new_task_1.title: Preserve Array API backends in xr.concat
new_task_1.description: The 2023.1.0 upgrade changes xarray concatenation so Array API-backed arrays are concatenated through their own array namespace rather than NumPy fallback logic. `xr.concat()` should preserve compatible non-NumPy array backends during concatenation instead of coercing results away from the active backend.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that concatenating xarray objects backed by Array API-compatible arrays uses the backend's native concat implementation so the result remains on that backend.

expectation.grounded: When xarray concatenation reaches `duck_array_ops.concatenate()` and the input arrays expose `__array_namespace__`, xarray must obtain the shared array namespace and call its `concat` operation on dtype-harmonized inputs. As a result, `xr.concat()` on compatible Array API-backed `DataArray` objects should return data backed by the same array ecosystem rather than falling back to NumPy concatenation.
expectation.conceptual: Concatenation should respect the active array backend. If users build xarray objects on an Array API implementation, combining them with `xr.concat()` should keep the computation in that backend and preserve the expected result type and values.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve existing dtype-promotion behavior by continuing to normalize inputs with shared-dtype logic before concatenation. NumPy-backed arrays should continue using the existing concatenation path, and the public `xr.concat()` API and result semantics must remain unchanged apart from backend preservation for Array API inputs.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve backend compatibility without changing how users call concat or altering the data values produced. Only the dispatch path should differ for Array API-capable inputs.

behavior: `xr.concat()` detects Array API-backed inputs through their array namespace support.
Concatenation uses the backend namespace's `concat` operation instead of NumPy fallback when those inputs are Array API-compatible.
The concatenated xarray result preserves an Array API-backed data container rather than coercing to a NumPy array.
Concatenated values and dimension semantics remain consistent with existing xarray concat behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When two `DataArray` objects backed by the same Array API-compatible backend are concatenated with `xr.concat(..., dim=...)`, the result should contain the correct concatenated values and shape.

When those inputs expose `__array_namespace__`, the result's `.data` should remain backed by the Array API implementation rather than being converted to a NumPy ndarray solely because of concatenation.
When NumPy-backed arrays are concatenated, xarray should continue to produce the same results as before the upgrade.
When concatenation requires dtype harmonization before combining inputs, the resulting values should still match xarray's existing shared-dtype concat semantics.
